card.name: Container
card.role: a program packaged with everything it needs to run

def.what: A program boxed together with everything it needs to run.
def.creator: A developer packages the program and its dependencies.
def.reader: Any machine that can run containers executes it.
def.where: On a server, in a data center or in the cloud.
def.analogy: A lunchbox: the food, the fork and the napkin in one box.

card.name: Kubernetes
card.role: runs and watches over containers on many machines

def.what: A program that runs and watches over huge numbers of containers across many machines.
def.creator: An operations team installs it on a set of servers.
def.reader: The containers it keeps running, and the teams that deploy them.
def.analogy: A building manager who decides which apartment each tenant gets.

card.name: Volume
card.role: a disk a program can read and write

def.what: A disk that a running program can write to and read from.
def.creator: Kubernetes asks a storage system to provide it.
def.where: On a storage system, attached to the machine running the program.
def.analogy: A notebook the program can write in, which survives a restart.

card.name: Storage system
card.role: provides the disks, in its own private language

def.what: Specialized hardware or software that stores data and provides disks.
def.creator: A storage vendor, or a team running storage software.
def.where: In the rack next to your servers, or as software on them.
def.analogy: A library that hands out and takes back notebooks.

card.name: Driver
card.role: translates between one system and one storage system

def.what: A program that translates between one system and one specific other system.
def.creator: The vendor or community that supports that pair.
def.reader: The system that needs the translation.
def.where: Running next to the software that uses it.
def.analogy: A printer driver: your laptop never learns every printer language.

card.name: Specification
card.role: a written contract both sides agree to follow

def.what: A written contract of the exact requests one side may make and the replies the other must give.
def.creator: A community of engineers writes and maintains it.
def.reader: Every engineer building either side of the contract.
def.where: A public document, usually versioned on GitHub.
def.analogy: The USB standard: any plug fits any socket because everyone follows it.

card.name: CNCF
card.role: the foundation that hosts Kubernetes and related projects

def.what: The Cloud Native Computing Foundation, a neutral foundation that hosts open source projects.
def.creator: The Linux Foundation created it.
def.reader: Projects like Kubernetes live under its umbrella.
def.where: An open community with public governance.
def.analogy: A neutral landlord for open source projects.

card.name: container-storage-interface/spec
card.role: the standard contract for storage plug-ins

def.what: The written standard that defines how any storage system can plug into container systems.
def.creator: A community of container and storage engineers.
def.reader: Every storage vendor that writes a driver.
def.where: A public repository of documents and API definitions.
def.analogy: The USB socket of the container world.

card.name: csi-addons/spec
card.role: extends CSI with replication and other requests

def.what: An extension of the CSI contract that adds requests CSI does not define.
def.creator: A community extending the original contract.
def.reader: Vendors that implement the extra requests.
def.where: A public repository, separate from CSI.
def.analogy: An appendix to a contract, not yet part of the law.

card.name: csi-addons/kubernetes-csi-addons
card.role: speaks the add-ons contract inside the cluster

def.what: The software that runs inside a Kubernetes cluster and implements the add-ons contract.
def.creator: The csi-addons community project.
def.reader: Programs on the cluster that need the extended storage requests.
def.where: Running inside the Kubernetes cluster, as a controller plus sidecars.
def.analogy: The switchboard operator on the cluster side of the contract.

card.name: ceph-csi / dell-csi / trident
card.role: vendor translators for real storage systems

def.what: The vendor programs that implement the contracts on the storage side.
def.creator: Storage vendors and communities, one per storage family.
def.where: Running inside the cluster, each talking to its own storage system.
def.analogy: One printer driver per printer brand.

def.what: A disaster recovery coordinator for workloads and their data across a pair of clusters.
def.creator: The RamenDR community project.
def.reader: It asks kubernetes-csi-addons for recovery operations.
def.where: Running on the clusters it protects.
def.analogy: The conductor that tells the storage orchestra when to switch sheets.

define.text: A small helper program that runs right next to a main program, packaged together with it.
A widely used way for two programs to call each other directly, like a phone line between pieces of software.
Keeping a second copy of data and workloads at another site, so a failed site can be brought back from that copy.
The coordinator that drives multi-step jobs automatically, instead of humans running them by hand.
